m: Masculine + uncountable → the de + le pair merges into one word.
LE gets EATEN. de + le is never written out.
f: Feminine + uncountable → de and la stay apart. Nothing merges.
LA ESCAPES. It never gets swallowed.
v: The noun starts with a vowel or a mute h, so la/le shrinks to l' — gender stops mattering.
Vowel ahead → the article gets out of the way.
p: Plural, so there is only one form. du and de la are singular words — they can never sit in front of a plural noun. Plural leaves you only des (some) or les (in general).
See an -S on the noun? DU is dead. Only DES or LES survive.
neg: After ne … pas, un / une / des / du / de la / de l' become de (d' before a vowel or mute h). le / la / les do NOT change (Je n'aime pas le café), and nothing changes after être (Ce n'est pas du pain).
DU, DE LA, DES, UN + PAS → DE. LE, LA, LES stay.
qty: A word that already says HOW MUCH kills the partitive — only bare de survives.
You already measured it → DE alone.
gen: aimer, adorer, détester, préférer talk about the thing in general, so they take the definite article, never a partitive.
LIKE IT → LE. TAKE IT → DU.
ah: This h is aspirate — an invisible wall. Nothing elides in front of it.
sans: sans already means 'without any', so no article follows it at all.
twin: This du is not a partitive — it is de + le meaning 'of the / about the', and it stays du after pas. Also jouer DE + instrument (jouer du piano, jouer de la guitare).
Same spelling, two jobs. Read the verb.
cnt: You can count this one, so it takes an indefinite article, not a partitive.
fix: A fixed expression. French pairs these activities and qualities with du / de la — learn each one as a lump.
faire du · avoir de la · il y a du — mug them up. (jouer is different: jouer DE + instrument.)
gre: Gender trap: a final -e tells you nothing. -ure is usually feminine (la confiture, la voiture), but other -re nouns must be learned one by one — le sucre, le beurre, le poivre, le verre are masculine, yet la fenêtre and la lettre are feminine.
Learn the article WITH the noun. Only -URE is a safe pattern.
t1: One man in the group and ILS wins.
t4: Definite article — 'the', or a thing in general.
t5: un · une · des, and after PAS they all become DE.
